observation_summary: The method `StringUtils.replaceEach` throws a NullPointerException when an element in the `searchList` or `replacementList` is null, because it attempts to call `.length()` on these elements without checking for nullity.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding a conditional check (`if (searchList[i] == null || replacementList[i] == null) { continue; }`) to validate the input data before performing operations that would otherwise trigger a NullPointerException. This is a classic case of missing input validation/guard logic.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows a NullPointerException at line 3676 in StringUtils.java.
Line 3676 performs `replacementList[i].length() - searchList[i].length()` without checking if either array element is null.
The fix diff adds a null check for both `searchList[i]` and `replacementList[i]` before accessing their length.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix modifies the loop, the root cause is the lack of a guard against null inputs, not an error in the computational logic itself.
